src._src: ClosedSource/DSX/Modules/Core/Rive/swift/RiveElement.swift (a .riv file: an http(s) url or a bundled name; the extension is optional)

artboard._src: OpenSource/Conformance/rive/selection.json (absent takes the file's default artboard, else the first; an unknown name is not_found)

stateMachine._src: OpenSource/Conformance/rive/selection.json (absent takes the artboard's first machine; naming this AND animation is refused as conflict)

animation._src: OpenSource/Conformance/rive/selection.json (plays a linear animation instead of a machine)

inputs._src: OpenSource/Conformance/rive/inputs.json (the bound object driving the machine's inputs: levels diffed, triggers fired on a value transition, an undeclared name refused)

autoplay._src: OpenSource/Conformance/rive/playback.json (autoplay=false mounts paused; a remount returns to this value)

fit._src: OpenSource/Conformance/rive/fit.json (cover | contain | fill | fitWidth | fitHeight | none; case and separators folded, an unknown word folds to contain and is diagnosed)

alignment._src: OpenSource/Conformance/rive/fit.json (nine positions plus the top/bottom/left/right edge-centre aliases)

ref._src: ClosedSource/DSX/Modules/Core/Rive/dsx.json (the imperative address for dsx.module.rive.*; defaults to src, and may be omitted in a call when exactly one <rive> is mounted)

a11yLabel._src: OpenSource/Conformance/rive/a11y.json (REQUIRED by lint_dsx when a gesture handler is bound: rive-a11y-label)

on:load._src: OpenSource/Conformance/rive/events.json ({artboard, stateMachine, animation, width, height} once the file has landed)

on:stateChange._src: OpenSource/Conformance/rive/events.json ({machine, state} on a real transition, never on an advance)

on:event._src: OpenSource/Conformance/rive/events.json ({name, properties} for a Rive event fired inside the animation; an openUrl event is data, never a navigation)

on:error._src: OpenSource/Conformance/rive/events.json ({code, message} over a closed code set)

notes: STATE-MACHINE animation, rendered by Rive's own runtime on every target (rive-ios, rive-android, @rive-app/canvas) - so pixels are the vendor's and are pinned nowhere. Everything AROUND the vendor is the shared kernel core (RiveCore.swift / RiveCore.kt / rive-core.ts, corpus OpenSource/Conformance/rive/) and IS pinned: the input fold and its trigger edges, the artboard/machine/animation selection and its refusals, fit and alignment, the playback and residency lifecycle, the payload shapes and the accessibility verdict. A timeline is <lottie>; a state machine is <rive>. Provided by the excludable Core/Rive module: with the module dropped the tag is unresolved, and on the NATIVE renderers its children render instead (the author's own fallback). The web renderer mounts its dsx-unsupported box for any unresolved tag and ignores the children today - the same behaviour <lottie> has there, and a cross-cutting mount.ts decision rather than this element's.
